Master Fali’s secular surname was Chen;

He was a descendant of Qun, the Minister of Works of the Jin dynasty.
From the Liang through to the Chen dynasties,

His ancestors and elder brothers had been successive patriarchs of the Confucian tradition for generations.
When the Dharma Master was young, he studied the *Sanlun* (Three Treatises),

He was extensively versed in all the scriptures;

Delighting in his elegant writings, he brings to light subtle and hidden truths;

Though appearing as if dull-witted or mute,

How could he merely be one whose conduct resembles that of Shan Tao and whose spirit is equal to that of Yu Liang?
His literary sentiments are indeed classical yet not vulgar, elegant yet governed by rule,

The five colors are employed to mutually proclaim [the truth].
In practicing the Way, one incorporates right view within the three emptinesses and rescues the multitude of deluded beings from the eight sufferings.
Having already mastered extensive learning while maintaining a humble mind,

He was truly a paragon of human ethics.
Furthermore, he provided relief to those in distress, prioritizing others over himself;
his noble reputation shone brightly upon the windows and doors of the forest.
Loving the mountains and waters that girdled him with mist and clouds,
his vows were such that he dissolved himself into obscurity and withdrew in leisurely seclusion. Thus,
at the end of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, he departed.
He concealed himself in Ghost Valley Cave on Mount Qingxi.
Its lofty structure of crags and cliffs obscures the sun and moon;
its open windows and doors breathe forth the wind and clouds.
In that time, he gathered the five fungi while reclining at ease;
he roamed through the eight dhyānas while resting;

Clad in *bìlì* garments upon the mountain slopes,

Yet its layered ridges and perilous peaks, its towering pines and vast ravines,

There was nothing he did not personally reach or witness with his own eyes, tracing every path and identifying every destination;

A Memorial to His Majesty on the Refutation of Heretical Treatises. Submitted by Fa Lin.
Having looked back deeply upon the origins of the Three Primal Powers and the Five Cycles, and the rise of the Celestial Sovereigns and Human Emperors:
The inscriptions of the tortoise diagram and the bird-script seal;
the canons of the golden tablets and vermilion caskets;
the measurements of the six cardinal lines and nine luminous rays.
Among the myriad scrolls of a hundred schools,
there are none that do not guide the way of human relations and the virtue of good faith,
nor fail to recount the teachings of the sovereigns Xun and Hua, as well as the Duke of Zhou and Confucius.
This summarizes its essential points.
It has not yet reached the source of birth and death;

To remain within the realm of existence and non-existence—how could this compare to the fivefold Dharma-body and the threefold clear knowledge of the seed-wisdom?
It is profoundly serene, eternally blissful; what change or transition could there be?
Profound indeed is True Suchness (Tathatā), neither arising nor ceasing;
yet it provides the sustenance for all myriad beings and extends its compassion to all spiritual powers,
opening the ferry to the other shore of liberation.
He opens the treasury of ultimate unconditionedness;
he pulls all living beings out from beyond the ocean of views;
he rescues his children from within the burning house.
Yet, the transformation [of the Dharma] has been separated from the Onion River for over a thousand years,
and the teaching has flowed into the land of Han for some six hundred years.
Stupas and niches stand in mutual view, and divine beings follow one after another.
Thus it was that Dao’an ascended the imperial carriage of the Qin Emperor,
and Senghui boarded the chariot of the Ruler of Wu;
the Dharma Master Gaozuo was able to expound upon the Eightfold Path.
The Buddhist Master was skillful in expounding the Five Vehicles;
his transformation of beings permeated the Nine Provinces, and his blessings moistened the Three Worlds.
Is this not what is meant by "benefiting all things"?
During the Sui dynasty, the mandate was stripped away and warhorses galloped across the outskirts.
Calamity arose from the four tyrants, and its poison flowed upon the common people.
Once the lamp of wisdom had faded, the rain of Dharma was about to cease.
It is thanks to our Great Tang,
which above responds to the will of Heaven and below accords with the aspirations of the common people,
repairing the heavens to beautify the three celestial images.
By stabilizing the earth, the Five Peaks were secured;
the people received the grace of a second creation,
and the Śākya school bore the gift of its renaissance.
Now we joyfully celebrate these six virtues and five constants, and those three sovereigns of antiquity;
they returned to the wind of primal simplicity and practiced the transformation of non-action.
I have observed that regarding the slanderous matters submitted by Fu Yi,
although they were not implemented by the authorities,
Yi nevertheless publicly disseminated them far and wide.
In human banquets and feasts, people compete in frivolous talk;
this brings ruin to pure refinement and truly defiles elegant customs.
Such superfluous things and false views damage the nation’s field of merit.
This is logically untenable.
We humbly observe that Your Highness has long relied upon the Three Refuges and been sustained by the Ten Wholesome Actions.
He has responded to the aspirations of the common people and fulfilled the destiny for the Great Treasure;
his Way accords with a period of great peace, and his virtue brings glory to the Empress.
When the resonance of successive thunder rolls forth, the burrows of all hibernating creatures open;
when the radiance of the rising sun and the brilliance of the fire illuminate, the dark alleys are all reflected as mirrors.
How magnificent! How truly so!
This is indeed difficult to name.
For this reason, Emperor Guangwu of the Han dynasty esteemed the world, and King Mu of Zhou sought eternal years;
yet you, moreover, have been able to humble your will before the gate of blessings and turn your thoughts toward the sublime realm.
With the ferry and the bridge ever in mind and the ramparts and moats as his heart’s concern,
I prostrate myself with the hope that you will topple the banner of false views and kindle the torch of the True Dharma.
That the transmission of the Image-Period transformation rests upon you is a source of profound fortune.
Unable to suppress my indignation and longing, I respectfully present these two fascicles of the *Poxie lun* (Treatise on Destroying Heresies).
I am deeply grieved that this work should thus intrude upon Your Majesty’s august presence.
I prostrate myself with increasing trepidation.
Respectfully submitted.

On the twenty-seventh day of the first month in the fifth year of the Wude era, the śramaṇa Shi Falin of Jifa Temple submits this. The Grand Historian, Court Dispersing Gentleman, Your Servant Fu Yi, presents eleven articles on the reduction of monasteries and stupas and the abolition of monks and nuns. Your Servant Yi states:
Your servant has heard that the reigns of Fuxi, Shennong, Xuanyuan, and Shun accorded with the spirit of Laozi and the Master of Li (Laozi). The *Shi* says:

"The superior uses the wind to transform the subordinate; the subordinate uses the wind to criticize the superior. Laozi served as a librarian in Zhou—equivalent to the modern Secretariat—and was originally not a Son of Heaven; how could he have possessed the transformative power of governance such that his rule would accord with that of Fuxi, Shennong, the August Sovereigns, or the rulers of Yu, Xia, Tang, and Zhou?

Regarding the statement that the governance accords with the teachings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, it says: "The Duke of Zhou and Confucius were both ministers of the state; they looked upward to the teachings of the Yu and Xia dynasties and downwardly transformed the corrupt and frivolous people. Furthermore, it was not the case that a true king could not act as a teacher himself; how could it be that the four sovereigns of Yu and Xia did not accord with the teachings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius? Although there may be a sequence in their sanctity, their moral virtue is no different."
Your Majesty possesses a transformative method of governance that prizes the principle of identifying with the superior.
I have heard that an eighty-year-old father beats the earth and sings,
while a fifteen-year-old youth drums upon his belly for joy.
Farmers yield the boundaries of their fields to one another, and travelers do not pick up what they find on the road.
Filial sons uphold their families, and loyal ministers fill the land.

Yet, when the ruler of the state faces peril, they sacrifice their lives to avenge him; the people say: "Since the entire state is filled with loyal ministers, how could there be such peril? They say: "The followers of the Six Ministers would never have dared to rise in rebellion. Furthermore, if a parent falls ill, the child attends to them by their side for the rest of their life.
Are these not the friends of Zeng Shen and Minzi?
Here, schools and academies form a forest;
they are the peers of Mo Di and General Geng Gong.

Xianglai Yu said in his memorial: "From the thirty-ninth generation down, there has been only one Zeng Shen; prior to Emperor Gao of Han, only Minzi was promoted. The words of Chenglin are unsubstantiated, and the memorial submitted by Yu is fundamentally hollow; the matter is taken too far."

Thus, there are those who preserve the Way and embody virtue, being without desire and without seeking; whereas Zhouyu and Shu段 could not preserve the Way, and Jie of Xia and Zhou of Yin were occupied solely with greed and seeking.

"Honor and disgrace are both attended by alarm. [The text] notes that Pan Chong served as an official at court; yet after Yi (the archer) was dead, he refused to feel alarm. Jishi and Yang Huo likewise held positions in the court ranks.
As for the cauldron atop Mount Jing, they climbed up to attach themselves to the ascending dragon.
At the altar of Guishi, they followed one another as they rode cranes;
the messengers of the Queen Mother of the West arrived with full ceremony to pay court,
and the spirits of the boundless blue seas came forth.
He traveled everywhere to pay court to the Emperor. The reason for this was that at that time, the teachings of Li (Laozi) and Kong (Confucius) were jointly revered.

[The opponent] argued: "The Yellow Emperor’s ascent of the dragon occurred during the era of the Three Sovereigns; the Queen Mother of the Jade Pool appeared again during the time of King Mu of Zhou. Calculating this, before Laozi had emerged and before Confucius existed, one should not instead have followed the teachings of Laozi and practiced the books of Confucius. Since there were no 'Hu' (barbarian) Buddhas, [the teachings of Laozi and Confucius] must be the ones. [The Master] rebuked him, saying: "Since you claim there are no Buddhas, it follows that there can be no Dao either. From the time of Emperor Ming of Han, when a golden man entered his dream while he slept at night..."
Fu Yi replied to the imperial decree, stating: "The barbarian deity is merely a puppet. If the Zhou dynasty had not sent for Fu Yi, how could he have known of the Buddha?

My lineage has long existed, and my ancestors spoke of the Buddha; you, on the contrary, claim there is none. As for the grave calamity of the five rebellious acts (*pañcānantarya*), from the beginningless kalpas until now, such things were unheard of in the Central Plains during the Later Han. The critic replied: "Your empty words are excessive. During the Wei and Jin dynasties, even the barbarians believed [in the Buddha] to some extent. Fu Yi replied: "As for ritual, music, and the scholar-official attire (*yiguan*), these were first fully established under the Jin dynasty. Since you slanderously call them 'barbarians,' who then was that person from the Central Kingdom named Ze Rong who used the pretext of Buddhist vegetarian feasts to incite rebellion?"
He fled to Jiangdong.
Lü Guang feigned an expedition against the Hu tribes to rebel against his sovereign.

[Daorong] stood firm in the western lands; some of his contemporaries envied him and slandered him, saying he had gathered a band of followers. When Lü Guang returned from his campaign, Fu Jian’s state was destroyed, and Daorong subsequently resided in the region west of the Yellow River, establishing a hegemony in Liangzhou. This was not because the monk rebelled and settled in the western lands, but rather occurred after these events.

The demonic Hu flourish and prevail, with more than half [of the population] mixed among the flowers; the "Admonition" says: "Purified by compassion, those who emerge in this final age of evil have the conditions for deliverance precisely at this time. Yet within the gates of the gentry, they instead receive shaven-headed men and heterodox precepts."

Among the scholars of the Confucian school, there are those who perversely utter the reckless words of the barbarians; their admonition says: "The gentry wear the robes of endurance, yet the Confucian scholar prizes the discourse of golden lips; these are as distorted as vulgar songs, and listening to them ruins one's fundamental nature."

If one passes by a stall of dried fish (*bào*) while smelling it, they lose their own fragrance; the critique says: "To emit such vomit-like sounds and waft such fishy stench—if one listens, one will surely know you have lost your fundamental nature. How could those who pass by not lose their fragrance? To look up and spit at heaven is to bring shame upon oneself; these words are indeed true. Furthermore, he extensively established monasteries, many of which were magnificent and varied. The critique says: "He performed the deeds that create rebirth in heaven and sowed the causes for liberation from suffering. He exhausted the labor of craftsmen while sitting alone amidst the mud and plaster. The critique further says: "He vied with his hands and body to fashion the images of the Holy Honored Ones, and struck the great bells of the Middle Kingdom."

A Censure on the False Multitude of Assembled Barbarian Monks: "They ring the divine bell refined a hundred times to summon the holy assembly of three thousand, moving the ears and eyes of the simple folk to seek out goods and bribes for their private gain.

A Censure on the Seeking of Private Wealth: "They appeal to the ears and eyes of those with faithful hearts to provoke the acquisition of wealth through greed and delusion—silk garments and fine brocades produced by women's crafts."
They are cut to form banners for licentious sacrifices.

Skillful artisans employ gold and silver to intricately carve the stupas for the śarīras. The admonition says: Female artisans fashion silks and brocades to create longevity banners; skillful craftsmen use gold and silver to erect mounds for the fragmented body. They provide fine rice, wheat, flour, and grain.
They have established assemblies for monks and nuns in a disorderly manner;

with fragrant oil and wax candles, they vainly illuminate the halls of barbarian spirits. The admonition says: "Rice, millet, flour, and grain are vied for and displayed at these 'fields of merit' assemblies; fragrant oil and wax candles are sought to illuminate the 'halls of compassion. Yet they plunder the people's wealth and deplete the state's reserves."
That the high ministers of the court have not once awakened to this truth is truly lamentable.

[The memorial] states: "The court examines antiquity and abandons the mundane to return to the True; it reveres the Buddhist community and does not share in heterodox views. We humbly beseech Your Majesty..."
He governs the opening and closing of the gates of the celestial realm and renews the precious throne;
he penetrates the stagnation and adversity of the myriad things.
He reared the common people of Qian,
spreading the wind of Laozi’s non-action so that the people transformed themselves spontaneously;
he upheld the rites of Confucius’s love and respect, so that the world became filial and compassionate.

Furthermore, the Buddha’s scriptural teachings falsely discourse upon sins and blessings; their admonitions state that they originate from the source of the teachings to show people the gateway for severing evil and to open the path for practicing goodness. Yet soldiers and commoners evade their duties by shaving their heads and hiding among the populace.

Failing to serve one's two parents while exclusively practicing the ten evils, the admonition says: "To abandon the affection and kindness of one's parents to cultivate the benevolent wind of the ten virtues—though one may tolerate minor transgressions to achieve great compliance, if years pass without removing such wickedness and falsehood, they will only become more extreme."
I have examined the written records from the time of Pao-xi down to Han Gaozu;
spanning twenty-nine generations and over four hundred sovereigns.

I have merely heard that at the suburban sacrifices to the Supreme Deity on Mount Yuanqiu, the Southern Suburb cannot avoid the fault of killing livestock; how could this compare to the Buddhist precept where non-killing is paramount? By weighing these matters, right and wrong become evident. As for governing the state and overseeing the people, I have yet to see a temple hall with bronze statues bring peace and stability to the nation through the establishment of such altars.

I request that the heretics of Hufo be ordered to return the Indian scriptures. The admonition states: "Things arise through conditions and cease once their purpose is served; coming and going respond to external objects, and appearing or disappearing according to the time. All śramaṇas shall be released to return to their native lands."
It shall cause those who evade taxes to universally delight in paying their rents,
and those who shirk labor service to likewise do so.

I have always delighted in offering my service. Do not, however, allow those shaven-headed and lowly men to merely bow with hands clasped before the state. It is said that in the past, Yan Zileng did not prostrate before the Son of Heaven, and Zhao Yuanshu bowed only with hands clasped before the Minister; the records praise their excellence. How much more so for śramaṇas, who are fields of merit transcending the world, and followers of Śākyamuni, who are high-minded gentlemen beyond mundane affairs? To compel them to pay formal obeisance would cause profound harm to the principles of propriety; it is simply unacceptable. As for providing loyal ministers to guard the ancestral temple, the Great Tang has already established its vast stability and acts as the sovereign of creation.

"The common people have no affairs; they are the subjects of the Sacrificial Sovereign (Xi Huang). [The Emperor] rebukes them, saying: 'In this age of Creation, the people do not pay taxes. The subjects of the Sacrificial Sovereign lie with drumming bellies. With such a sagely and enlightened ruler above, how can he believe the words of Cui Hao and Jiang Bin? Your servant Yi is truly prostrate with fear and awe. [The Emperor] rebukes him, saying: "To serve one's lord, exhaust one's loyalty; in speech, there must be sincerity. If what is reported to the throne is untrue, the guilt shall fall upon the offender. To slander the state, one must ultimately submit to the sword. How can mere fear and awe suffice? This is respectfully submitted."
